text:
1. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` — correctness: `inline_function_parameters` only checks `usage.callee_count == call_sites.len()`, but a function's identifier can be referenced in non-call positions (passed as a value, assigned, exported-via-reference, recursive call, used in `typeof`, etc.) without necessarily setting `USED_AS_REF`/`REASSIGNED` in every such path. More critically, nothing checks that the identifier isn't also bound/shadowed by an inner scope with the same `Id`-independent name, or that there's exactly one declaration site (function could be reassigned to a different function value while keeping same binding, e.g. `function f(){} f = other;` — `REASSIGNED` flag is checked on the fn var, but there's no check that `usage.ref_count` corresponds only to calls, i.e. no guard against the function being passed around and invoked indirectly through an alias that creates a new call site not captured by `record_call_site_args` — in that case `call_sites.len()` would legitimately be less than actual invocations, silently causing unsound "all call sites known" reasoning if an alias calls it too). Fix: require that total `ref_count` (minus the call sites themselves) is zero, i.e. the identifier is *only* ever used as a direct callee, never captured as a value — the PR description claims this ("no aliasing, passing as value") but the implementation doesn't verify it anywhere in `params.rs`.

2. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` (`apply_param_inlining` / `remove_inlined_call_args`) — correctness: call-site argument removal is driven by a separate, later pass (`inlined_params` map consulted in `visit_mut_call_expr`) rather than being done atomically with the parameter removal. Between the two mutations, if a call site has fewer args than the removed index (e.g. `complex("foo")` already omits `fn`), `remove_inlined_call_args` just skips (`if idx < call.args.len()`), which is fine, but if a call site passes an argument for a *trailing* inlined param and an argument for a *later, non-inlined* param in the same call is index-shifted incorrectly because indices are computed against the original (pre-inlining) parameter list while `call.args` may have a different length per call site — removing by raw index without accounting for argument-count mismatches per call site can delete the wrong argument. This needs a test with heterogeneous arg counts per call site (e.g. one call omitting args, another providing extra) to confirm correctness, and currently there is none.

3. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` — scope/hygiene bug: the generated `const` declarations reuse `ident.clone()` (the parameter's `Ident`, including its original `SyntaxContext`) directly as the new variable's binding. If the function also declares a local variable, nested function, or has a parameter later in the list with a colliding name under a different context, or if the inlined value expression itself references identifiers from the *call-site* scope (e.g. a call site passes a reference to a call-site-local const — though restricted to literals today per `is_safe_constant_for_param_inline`, this restriction is the only thing preventing scope-capture bugs and is fragile: nothing stops a future "safe constant" from being extended to include identifiers without re-deriving hygiene), this is a latent hygiene trap. At minimum, add a check/comment that `common_value` must not contain any `Ident` (not just restrict by literal shape) to prevent reintroducing scope bugs when the safe-value list is extended later.

4. `crates/swc_ecma_usage_analyzer/src/analyzer/mod.rs` (`visit_call_expr`) — performance: this clones every call argument expression (`arg.expr.clone()`) for every call site of every identifier-callee call, unconditionally, even when the callee has no chance of being optimized (e.g. called many times with different values, or not a function declared in this module). This is confirmed by CodSpeed to cause a 3–8% regression across benchmarks. Needs a cheap early-out — e.g. only start recording once we already know values differ is moot, but at minimum gate behind whether `options.inline` (or similar) is active, or record cheaply-comparable argument fingerprints instead of cloning full ASTs, deferring the clone until a match is actually needed.

5. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/program_data.rs` (`call_site_args` field / `record_call_site_args`) — memory/perf: `Vec<Vec<Option<Box<Expr>>>>` is unconditionally accumulated for every call of every named function in the program for the lifetime of the whole analysis pass, even for hot functions called thousands of times (e.g. lodash internals) where the data is never going to qualify (values differ after the second call). There's no early abandonment: once two call sites disagree, storage should stop growing. Fix: track a "still a candidate" bool per function and stop recording/allocating once disqualified, or cap based on `callee_count` already known to be irrelevant.

6. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` — this pass is invoked unconditionally inside `visit_mut_fn_decl`/`visit_mut_fn_expr` (one new mod, wired straight into existing hot traversal) rather than gated by a distinct `CompressOptions` flag. Repurposing `options.inline` (an existing, differently-scoped setting for inlining IIFEs/simple functions) to also toggle this unrelated and currently-regressing optimization conflates two independent knobs and gives users no way to disable just the expensive new pass while keeping existing `inline` behavior. Add a dedicated option (e.g. `inline_params` or similar) defaulting to off until performance is fixed, consistent with project convention of flag-gating optimizer passes.

7. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` (`is_safe_constant_for_param_inline` / `expr_eq`) — unary case allows `UnaryOp::Minus` and `Bang` with recursive safety check, but `expr_eq`'s corresponding unary branch compares only `op_a == op_b` and recurses — this is fine for structural equality, but `is_safe_constant_for_param_inline` doesn't restrict the *inner* literal type meaningfully (e.g. `-"str"` or `!{}` aren't expressible since arg must already be Lit recursively, so acceptable) — minor, but the pair of functions duplicate logic that should be unified into one "normalize to canonical constant" representation to avoid future divergence bugs (e.g. someone extends one but not the other). Low severity but worth flagging as a maintenance hazard before merge.

8. Fixture tests (`tests/fixture/param_inline/arrow_function/`) — the PR's own description lists only `basic` and `different_values` as added, but the diff also includes `arrow_function`, `literal_values`, `mixed_params`, `multiple_params` with expected outputs that assume this pass runs for arrow functions — yet the integration hook in `mod.rs` only wires `inline_function_parameters` into `visit_mut_fn_decl` and `visit_mut_fn_expr`, not arrow functions. The `arrow_function/output.js` fixture expecting inlining to happen is therefore asserting behavior the code doesn't implement; this test is either currently failing or not actually exercising the new code path (silently passing because nothing changes, matching `different_values`-style no-op) — needs verification and is exactly the "test output inconsistency" flagged by the earlier automated review but not yet fixed in this diff.

9. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` (`remove_inlined_call_args`) — only matches `Callee::Expr(Expr::Ident(..))`; calls through `this.method()`, optional chaining call (`fn?.()`), or re-exported/aliased bindings to the same function are never cleaned up, leaving the function permanently mismatched in arity vs. its remaining call sites if such a call site exists but wasn't counted in `callee_count` the same way — combined with concern #1, this is the main correctness gap: the set of call sites used to *decide* inlining (via `call_site_args`/`callee_count`) and the set of call sites actually *patched* afterward (via `remove_inlined_call_args`, identifier-callee-only) are not guaranteed to be the same set, which can leave a stale/too-many-args call against an arity-reduced function.

10. `crates/swc_ecma_minifier/src/compress/optimize/params.rs` — no handling for `Function.length`/`arguments.length`-sensitive code, `fn.toString()`, or higher-order use of the function reference (e.g. `.apply`, `.call`, `.bind`) elsewhere in the same program that could pass more/fewer arguments at runtime than the static call sites seen; given this is a correctness-sensitive minifier change (silently altering program semantics), this should at minimum be covered by a code comment and test demonstrating it's out of scope, consistent with project convention (AGENTS.md "write unit tests for your code").
